tier_reason: Upgraded from B. The HN page has no numbers, so benchmark_url now points to the official TechEmpower Round 20 physical-environment results JSON. That file has per-test totals for lithium-postgres-batch, actix-core and actix-pg, all run on Citrine hardware (Intel Xeon Gold 5120). The benchmark code is public in TechEmpower/FrameworkBenchmarks: frameworks/C++/lithium/lithium_batch.cc and compile-batch.sh, plus frameworks/Rust/actix/actix-core.dockerfile. At Round-20-era commit 68c13b5c, the build files state clang from buildpack-deps:focal (LLVM 10, called as llvm-profdata-10) with -O3 -march=native -flto -std=c++17 plus two-pass PGO. The actix build states rust:1.44 with RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native" cargo build --release.

corrections.baseline: actix-web (best TechEmpower actix implementation in Round 20, actix-core; also actix-pg). H2O is a secondary comparison from the author's own statement.
corrections.claimed_speedup: TechEmpower Round 20, the official run on Citrine physical hardware, completed 2021-01-04. Best responses/sec per test comes from the results JSON (derived from page data). lithium-postgres-batch vs actix-core: single query 833,811 vs 635,092 (1.31x); 20 queries 59,452 vs 34,956 (1.70x); updates at 20 queries 34,888 vs 24,301 (1.44x); Fortunes 618,610 vs 653,529 (0.95x, slower). JSON is 1,599,157 (lithium-postgres-beta) vs 1,563,587 (actix-raw), 1.02x. Plaintext is about 7.00M for both (network-bound tie). lithium-postgres-batch had the top single-query result of all implementations and was second in 20-query and updates. The earlier HN post (2020-08-29) only says in its title that Lithium 'ranked the highest performance web application platform' in a continuous run's composite view; it gives no rps numbers. On HN the author said non-batched Lithium is 'as fast (slighly faster on some tests, slighly slower on others)' as H2O. One commenter wrote '2x faster than the Actix Rust framework', which is unverified.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: TechEmpower Round-20-era build (FrameworkBenchmarks commit 68c13b5c, 2020-11-11): lithium-postgres-batch.dockerfile uses buildpack-deps:focal and apt clang (LLVM 10, called as llvm-profdata-10). compile-batch.sh builds lithium_batch.cc with clang++ -O3 -march=native -flto -std=c++17 -DNDEBUG -DN_SQL_CONNECTIONS=1 and two-pass PGO (-fprofile-instr-generate, then -fprofile-instr-use). It links a patched libpq (compile_libpq.sh batchmode), and the Lithium single headers are pinned at commit 10b72ad8. Baseline actix-core: FROM rust:1.44, RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native" cargo build --release.
corrections.hardware: TechEmpower Citrine (rounds 16-22): three Dell R440 servers (application, database, load generator), each with an Intel Xeon Gold 5120 CPU, 32 GB RAM and an enterprise SSD, on a dedicated Cisco 10-gigabit Ethernet switch. The August 2020 continuous run 57b25c85 also ran on Citrine.
corrections.caveats: The Round 20 win depends on the libpq pipelining/batch variant (lithium-postgres-batch). On 2022-05-31 TechEmpower removed these tests (PR #7382) 'to comply with the benchmark rules'. In later official data Lithium is slower than actix on database tests. Round 21 vs actix-http: single query 377,722 vs 512,831 (0.74x); 20 queries 0.66x; Fortunes 0.75x; updates 0.73x. Round 22: 0.82x, 0.80x, 0.86x and 0.91x on the same tests (derived from page data). In Rounds 22-23 Lithium is also below H2O on all database tests. It is only equal to or slightly above actix on JSON and plaintext. Brian from TechEmpower cautioned on HN that the August 2020 continuous run (57b25c85, TFB commit 4a00589b) had not received official-round sanity checking and 'should be taken with a grain of salt'. That run's results data is not archived: tfb-status.techempower.com is unreachable, and Wayback holds only the status page, not results.json. The HN thread's remark about actix is from commenter The_rationalist, not the author, and says the opposite of the earlier record: actix-web DID benefit from query pipelining because tokio-postgres is its own implementation and does not use libpq. The README still says Lithium is 'ranked #1 on the TechEmpower benchmark (composite score)'; this is out of date. TechEmpower/FrameworkBenchmarks was archived on 2026-03-24. Linux-only (epoll).

notes: Metadata confirmed via gh GraphQL, because REST returned a 403 rate limit: MIT license, not a fork, not archived, 1,409 stars, last commit 2026-07-31 (active). Round 20 per-test numbers are best rps per implementation computed from the rawData totalRequests over the 15 s runs. The composite score could not be recomputed because TechEmpower sets per-round weights that are not published in the JSON. The entry is a real, notable win against actix-web, but only in 2020 to early 2021, with the pipelined database variant, and it did not last. Consider tagging it as a historical result.
